items.followUp: State two important purposes of biological classification.

rubric.why: Taxonomy identifies, names and classifies organisms.
rubric.description: Gives an aim of taxonomy: identification, naming or classification of organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one of these aims.

rubric.why: Systematics considers relationships among organisms, including their evolutionary relationships.
rubric.description: States that systematics studies relationships among organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying relationships, especially evolutionary relationships.

modelAnswer: Taxonomy aims to identify, name and classify organisms.
Systematics studies the diversity of organisms and their relationships, including their evolutionary relationships.

items.followUp: What is a malignant tumour, and how can it affect other parts of the body?

rubric.why: A benign tumour remains confined to its original site.
rubric.description: States that a benign tumour is localized and does not invade or spread to other tissues.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that it remains at its site and does not spread.

rubric.why: Benign tumours do not behave like invasive cancers and are usually not life-threatening.
rubric.description: States that a benign tumour is non-cancerous or usually not life-threatening.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the non-cancerous or usually harmless nature.

modelAnswer: A benign tumour is an abnormal mass of cells that remains localized at its original site.
It does not invade nearby tissues or spread to other parts of the body, and is usually not life-threatening.

items.followUp: What important events occur during the S phase of the cell cycle?

rubric.why: G1 is the first growth phase of interphase, following mitosis and preceding DNA synthesis.
rubric.description: Identifies G1 as the first growth phase after mitosis and before DNA replication.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct position or identification of G1.

rubric.why: During G1, the cell grows and produces proteins and organelles needed for its activities and later stages.
rubric.description: Describes cell growth and the synthesis of proteins or organelles during G1.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for cell growth and at least one relevant synthesis/activity.

modelAnswer: G1 is the first growth phase of interphase, occurring after mitosis and before DNA replication.
The cell grows and synthesizes proteins and organelles needed for its normal activities and preparation for DNA replication.

items.followUp: Describe how cytokinesis occurs in plant cells.

rubric.why: In animal cells, a contractile ring causes the cell membrane to form a cleavage furrow.
rubric.description: Names the contractile ring or cleavage furrow formed during animal-cell cytokinesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the furrow or its contractile ring.

rubric.why: The furrow deepens and divides the cytoplasm into two daughter cells.
rubric.description: Explains that the furrow moves inward and separates the cytoplasm into two cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the inward pinching and resulting division.

modelAnswer: A contractile ring forms beneath the cell membrane and creates a cleavage furrow.
The furrow pinches inward until the cytoplasm is divided into two daughter cells.

items.followUp: Define a limiting factor and name two factors that limit the rate of photosynthesis.

rubric.why: A limiting factor restricts the rate of a process when its availability is insufficient or below the optimum.
rubric.description: Defines a limiting factor as one that restricts the rate of a process when insufficient or below optimum.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition.

rubric.why: Light intensity is a recognised limiting factor of photosynthesis.
rubric.description: Names light intensity as a limiting factor of photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming light intensity.

rubric.why: Carbon dioxide concentration and temperature are also limiting factors of photosynthesis.
rubric.description: Names carbon dioxide concentration or temperature as another limiting factor.
rubric.how: This is included as an additional accepted example within the names mark; do not award marks beyond the question total.

modelAnswer: A limiting factor is a factor whose insufficient availability restricts the rate of a process.
The main limiting factors of photosynthesis are light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration and temperature.

items.followUp: Explain how an enzyme's active site helps it catalyse a reaction.

rubric.why: The active site binds a specific substrate to form an enzyme-substrate complex.
rubric.description: States that the active site binds the substrate specifically.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for substrate binding or formation of the enzyme-substrate complex.

rubric.why: The enzyme catalyses the reaction at the active site, converting substrate into product.
rubric.description: States that the active site enables the reaction, producing products or lowering activation energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the catalytic function.

modelAnswer: The active site has a specific shape that binds the enzyme's substrate, forming an enzyme-substrate complex.
It catalyses the reaction, converting the substrate into products.

items.followUp: How can a change in temperature affect an enzyme's activity?

rubric.why: Denaturation changes the enzyme's three-dimensional shape, including the shape of its active site.
rubric.description: States that denaturation alters the enzyme's shape or active site.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the structural change.

rubric.why: With its active site altered, the enzyme cannot bind its substrate properly and loses catalytic activity.
rubric.description: Explains that the altered active site prevents normal substrate binding or enzyme activity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the resulting loss of function.

modelAnswer: Denaturation is a change in an enzyme's three-dimensional shape, including the shape of its active site.
The substrate can no longer bind properly, so the enzyme loses its catalytic activity.

items.followUp: What is the role of hydrochloric acid in the stomach during protein digestion?

rubric.why: Hydrochloric acid in the stomach activates inactive pepsinogen.
rubric.description: Identifies hydrochloric acid as the substance that converts pepsinogen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming hydrochloric acid or HCl.

rubric.why: The conversion produces active pepsin from inactive pepsinogen.
rubric.description: States that pepsinogen is converted into active pepsin.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct conversion.

modelAnswer: Hydrochloric acid (HCl) in the stomach converts inactive pepsinogen into active pepsin.
Pepsin can also activate more pepsinogen.
